rules: R1 (SH-01, street seating): the guide lists "terrace" as an example of a cafe exterior, so outdoor seating counts when cafe furniture (tables/chairs with drinks) set out on the street/pavement is visible from the street. A street or crowd with no cafe furniture, storefront, sign or facade does not count ("Not any street"). A logo on glass seen from inside, with interior behind it, is not "visible from the street".

R2 (SH-09, capsule machine): the guide defines extracting as "coffee flowing from the group head / portafilter". A capsule machine has neither, so its flow into a cup is not SH-09 (it can still be SH-05). Coffee visibly emerging from a portafilter basket (including a bottomless portafilter before a single stream forms) counts.

R3 (SH-11, barista/worker): read literally, the person must be identifiable as a barista or worker: a commercial counter, cafe/restaurant service setting or commercial machine in the shot. Home brewers, ceremony performers or hosts with no service context, and hands-only tutorials in domestic or studio settings do not count. The person must also be preparing coffee (grinding, tamping, operating the machine, pouring); rinsing a pitcher or presenting a finished cup does not count. A partly visible worker (hands) counts when the setting is commercial.

R4 (SH-08): a person counts when a clearly distinct body is visible (face, torso, or a limb that clearly belongs to a second person, e.g. an arm reaching across the counter). The setting must be the inside of a cafe/coffee shop. Frames are judged through glass or dissolves when the people are clearly discernible.

R5 (SH-06 vs SH-05): SH-06 is negative when anything is visibly being poured or dripped into the cup/glass, applying "not being poured into" literally (this includes sugar), and when the cup is held or lifted in the hands rather than standing on a table, saucer or counter. A cup resting on a surface with a hand still touching it counts. Any visible stream or drip of coffee/milk into a cup counts for SH-05, whatever the machine.

R6 (SH-03): "fill a clear part of the frame, close up" means the beans are a close-up, dominant element. Beans that take up a small part of a medium or wide shot (in a bowl, cup or small glass) do not count.
R7 (dissolves/split screens): judge only what is clearly discernible in the frame; a layer that clearly shows the requirement counts.
R8 (SH-04): grinding must be evident from the still, with ground coffee visibly coming out of the spout. A finger on the button, an idle grinder, or residue at the spout does not count.

Brand (SH-10_brand_readable): judged on the coffee packages themselves. "Douwe Egberts" is clearly readable on a cardboard collection box for D.E points (t=20-25, 84-86), but that box is not a package of coffee. On the green coffee packs (t=0-4, 20-25, 41-47, 84-86) only a round logo seal is visible and no brand text can be read, so the answer is "no".
